gaps.detail: ACC Lemma 7.1.3 facts (1)–(5) hold over the algebraic closure and fact (6) is the RG2.0a Weil restriction computation; facts (7)–(8) need Galois descent of forms (Aut(PGL₂^r) = PGL₂^r ⋊ S_r), the classification of forms by H¹(Q_l, Aut PGL₂^r), and the statement that a form which is quasi-split and split over an unramified extension is ∏_i Res_{N_i/Q_l} PGL₂ with N_i/Q_l unramified. No atlas layer owns the Galois cohomology and forms of reductive groups: the upstream ReductiveGroups layers 7–9 give structure, split classification and pinned automorphisms, AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 has torsors and Kneser’s theorem for simply connected groups only, and the PELModuli packet records the same missing owner for its twisting classification. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0 transports conjugacy under inner twists but does not classify forms. The accepted candidate ReductiveGroupsArithmeticPartII (arithmetic forms and cohomological transfer) is the natural owner; the restructure proposal asks that its brief include this classification. Until it exists the closure of the three consuming declarations rests on this gap.

sourceCoverage.name: Weyl groups W(G,T), W_P(G,T), dominant cones and the Kostant representatives W^P(G,T)
sourceCoverage.statement: For the Siegel Levi GL_n×GL_n in GL_{2n}, define KostantShuffle(n) as permutations w of {0,…,2n−1} whose inverse is increasing on each block {0,…,n−1} and {n,…,2n−1}. These are the minimal representatives for (S_n×S_n)\S_{2n}; length is the number of inversions of w. For Res_{F⁺/Q} use one shuffle per embedding and sum lengths. General Weyl groups, roots, dominant weights and highest-weight modules are imported, not defined here.

sourceCoverage.name: Hecke algebras of positive monoids (§2.1.9) and Lemma 2.1.10
sourceCoverage.statement: Local setting: F non-archimedean with residue field of cardinality q, G reductive over F. For U ⊂ G(F) open compact and Δ ⊂ G(F) an open submonoid with UΔU = Δ, ℋ(Δ, U) ⊂ ℋ(G(F), U) (functions supported in Δ) is a subalgebra, and for an R[Δ]-module (or complex) M there is ℋ(Δ,U) → End_{𝐃(R)}(RΓ(U, M)). Let P = MN be a parabolic with opposite P̄ = MN̄ and U admit an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P: with U_N = U ∩ N(F), U_M = U ∩ M(F), U_N̄ = U ∩ N̄(F), both product maps U_N × U_M × U_N̄ → U and U_N̄ × U_M × U_N → U are bijective. Δ_M = {t ∈ M(F) : tU_Nt^{-1} ⊂ U_N and U_N̄ ⊂ tU_N̄t^{-1}} (U-positive elements), Δ = U_NΔ_MU_N̄. Lemma 2.1.10: Δ_M and Δ are monoids, Δ_M is open in M(F), Δ is open in G(F), UΔU = Δ and Δ ∩ M(F) = Δ_M. Hence ℋ(Δ,U), ℋ(Δ_M,U_M) are defined, Δ_P = Δ ∩ P(F) is a monoid and ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) is defined.

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 2.1.11: restriction and integration are algebra homomorphisms on monoid Hecke algebras; basis formulas
sourceCoverage.statement: The maps r_P : ℋ(Δ,U) → ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) (restriction to P(F)) and r_M : ℋ(Δ_P,U_P) → ℋ(Δ_M,U_M) (integration along U_N) are algebra homomorphisms. On basis elements, for m ∈ Δ_M, r_P([UmU]) = [U_PmU_P] and 𝒮([UmU]) := r_M∘r_P([UmU]) = #(U_N/mU_Nm^{-1})[U_MmU_M] = |δ_P(m)|_F^{-1}[U_MmU_M].

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 2.1.14: Hecke-equivariant evaluation map on invariants of an induced module, with functorial R-splitting
sourceCoverage.statement: Let R be a ring, W an R[P(F)]-module and V = Ind_{P(F)}^{G(F)} W. There is a natural morphism φ : V^U → r_P^*W^{U_P} of ℋ(Δ,U) ⊗_ℤ R-modules (f ↦ f(1)), and, writing (?)^∼ for the forgetful functor to R-modules, (V^U)^∼ → (r_P^*W^{U_P})^∼ has a functorial splitting: for representatives g₁ = 1, g₂, …, g_n of P(F)\G(F)/U, V^U ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^n W^{g_iUg_i^{-1}∩P(F)} via f ↦ (f(g_i))_i.

sourceCoverage.name: Global split morphisms relating G-, P- and M-cohomology with monoid Hecke actions
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a number field, G reductive over F, P = MN a parabolic, and K_G = K_{G,S}K_{G,T}K_G^{T∪S} good where T, S are disjoint finite sets of finite places, G_{F_v} is unramified and K_v hyperspecial for v ∉ S ∪ T, and K_{G,v} has an Iwahori decomposition w.r.t. P for v ∈ T (monoids Δ_{G,v}, Δ_{G,T} = ∏_{v∈T}Δ_{G,v}, and Δ_{P,T}, Δ_{M,T}). Then 𝒮 : ℋ(G^{S∪T} × Δ_{G,T}, K_G^S) → ℋ(M^{S∪T} × Δ_{M,T}, K_M^S), and for a ring R: (i) there is a split morphism RΓ([Ind_{P^∞}^{G^∞}𝔛_P]/K_G, R) → RΓ(X^P_{K_P}, R) in 𝐃(R), equivariant for ℋ(G^{S∪T} × Δ_{G,T}, K_G^S) ⊗ R (acting on the target via r_P; [NT16, Cor. 2.6], Lemma 2.1.14), whence a surjection H*([Ind 𝔛_P]/K_G, R) → r_P^*H*(X^P_{K_P}, R) of Hecke modules (the splitting need not be equivariant); (ii) there is a split morphism RΓ(X^M_{K_M}, R) → RΓ(X^P_{K_P}, R) in 𝐃(R), equivariant for ℋ(P^{S∪T} × Δ_{P,T}, K_P^S) ⊗ R acting on the source via r_M [NT16, Prop. 3.4].

sourceCoverage.name: Dominant weights, algebraic representations and integral dual-Weyl lattices 𝒱_λ for G = Res GL_n
sourceCoverage.statement: Fix a prime p and a finite E/ℚ_p in Q̄_p containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p, with ring of integers 𝒪 and uniformizer ϖ. For Ω of characteristic 0 with #Hom(F,Ω) = [F:ℚ], identify X*((Res_{F⁺/ℚ}T)_Ω) = (ℤⁿ)^{Hom(F,Ω)} via (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_Ω = ∏_{τ∈Hom(F,Ω)}GL_n and (λ₁,…,λ_n) ↦ (diag(t₁,…,t_n) ↦ t₁^{λ₁}⋯t_n^{λ_n}); the Res_{F⁺/ℚ}(B ∩ G)_Ω-dominant weights form (ℤⁿ₊)^{Hom(F,Ω)} = {(λ_{τ,i}) : λ_{τ,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ λ_{τ,n} for all τ}. V_λ = ⊗_τ V_{λ_τ} is the algebraic representation of (Res_{F/ℚ}GL_n)_Ω of highest weight λ; λ^∨_{τ,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i}, and V_λ^∨ ≅ V_{λ^∨} (not for the lattices below without further hypotheses). For Ω = E, 𝒱_{λ_τ} ⊂ V_{λ_τ} is the GL_n(𝒪)-stable lattice of [Ger19, §2.2] (M_{λ_τ} there), the integral dual Weyl module of highest weight λ_τ (global sections of a line bundle on the full flag variety), and 𝒱_λ = ⊗_τ 𝒱_{λ_τ}, an 𝒪[∏_{v|p}GL_n(𝒪_{F_v})]-module, finite free over 𝒪.

sourceCoverage.name: Weights for G̃, the weight dictionary λ ↦ λ̃ (2.2.2), and the integral lattices 𝒱_λ̃
sourceCoverage.statement: For descending Levi rows λ_τ and λ_{τc} of length n and a chosen lift τ above an embedding of F⁺, define the unitary row by concatenating −reverse(λ_{τc}) with λ_τ. It is descending exactly when −λ_{τc,1}≥λ_{τ,1}. This is the character-lattice identification (2.2.2); it does not assert that the integral dual-Weyl lattice is the dual of the integral lattice of the dual weight.

sourceCoverage.name: Iwahori-level operators U_{v,i}, U_v, ⟨u⟩ for GL_n, the monoid Δ_p, the character α_λ and the twisted action ·_p on 𝒱_λ
sourceCoverage.statement: Standing data: F a CM field, n ≥ 1, p a prime, E/Q_p finite containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p; standing hypothesis for all of §5: F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits (p may ramify in F). Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, S a finite set of finite places of F containing S_p and stable under c, such that (i) for every finite v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (ii) K_v = Iw_v for v | p and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for finite v ∉ S. For integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, K(b,c) ⊂ K is the good subgroup with K(b,c)_v = K_v for v ∤ p and K(b,c)_v = Iw_v(b,c) for v | p; K(0,1) = K and K(0,c)/K(b,c) ≅ ∏_{v|p} T_n(O_{F_v}/ϖ_v^b). Define T^{S,ord} = T^S ⊗_O O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧[{U_{v,1},…,U_{v,n},U_{v,n}^{-1}}_{v|p}] (U_{v,i} formal variables), U_v = U_{v,1}U_{v,2}⋯U_{v,n−1}, U_p = ∏_{v|p} U_v. The canonical surjection O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧ → O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)] extends to T^{S,ord} → End_{D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)])}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)), U_{v,i} acting by the double coset operator [Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) Iw_v(b,c)] (i entries ϖ_v). Additional standing hypothesis for §§5.2–5.5: ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c for every v | p; the U_{v,i} depend on ϖ_v but RΓ^ord, T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord and the truth of Theorem 5.5.1 do not.

sourceCoverage.name: Iwahori-level operators Ũ_{v,i}, Ũ_v, ⟨u⟩ for G̃, the monoid Δ̃_p and the twisted action on 𝒱_λ̃
sourceCoverage.statement: Every p-adic place of F^+ splits in F; the fixed lifts ṽ ∈ S̃_p give ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p} ι_ṽ: G̃(F_p^+) ≅ ∏_{v̄∈S̄_p} GL_{2n}(F_ṽ), with T ⊂ B ⊂ G̃ corresponding to T_{2n} ⊂ B_{2n}. T̃^{S,ord} = T̃^S ⊗_O O⟦T(O_{F^+,p})⟧[{Ũ_{v,1},…,Ũ_{v,2n},Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1}}_{v∈S_p}] / (Ũ_{v^c,i} − Ũ_{v,2n−i} Ũ_{v,2n}^{-1})_{v∈S_p, i=1,…,2n}; Ũ_v = [Iw diag(ϖ^{2n−1},…,ϖ,1) Iw] (equivalently the product of the 2n−1 simple ordinary operators with the source normalization) and Ũ_p = ∏_{v∈S_p} Ũ_v. For K̃ good with K̃_v̄ = Ĩw_v̄ (v̄ ∈ S̄_p) and c ≥ b ≥ 0, c ≥ 1: K̃(b,c)_v̄ = K̃_v̄ (v̄ ∉ S̄_p), Ĩw_v̄(b,c) (v̄ ∈ S̄_p). For λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F^+,E)} there is a well-defined direct summand RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃)^ord on which Ũ_p acts invertibly, and T̃(K̃(b,c),λ̃)^ord := T̃^{S,ord}(RΓ_{K̃(0,c)/K̃(b,c)}(X̃_{K̃(b,c)}, V_λ̃)^ord). Monoids: T(F_p^+)^+ ⊂ T(F_p^+) = elements contracting N(O_{F^+,p}); under T(F_p^+) = T_n(F_p), T(F_p^+)^+ ⊂ T_n(F_p)^+ (strictly for n ≥ 2); Ĩw_p(b,c) = ∏_{v̄} Ĩw_v̄(b,c); Δ̃_p = Ĩw_p(b,c) T(F_p^+)^+ Ĩw_p(b,c) with its ·_p-action on V_λ̃; T(O_{F^+,p})(b) = T_n(O_{F,p})(b); B(O_{F^+,p})(b) = preimage of T(O_{F^+,p})(b) in B(O_{F^+,p}); B(F_p^+)^+ = N(O_{F^+,p})·T(F_p^+)^+.

sourceCoverage.name: Theorem 2.4.2 (non-Eisenstein localization of the boundary sees only the Siegel stratum)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let K̃, K be as in §2.4.1 (K̃ good, decomposed with respect to P = GU; S = S^c), let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S, and λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)}. sourceCoverage.name: Theorem 2.4.4 (𝒮 descends to boundary and GL_n Hecke algebras with coefficients)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let K̃ be as in §2.4.1 (good, decomposed with respect to P = GU; K = K̃ ∩ G(A^∞_{F⁺})), let λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)} be dominant with image λ̃ ∈ (Z^{2n})^{Hom(F⁺,E)} (under (2.2.2)) G̃-dominant, let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K, λ) be non-Eisenstein and 𝔪̃ = 𝒮*(𝔪) ⊂ T̃^S. sourceCoverage.statement: With K̃ decomposed (so K̃_P = K̃_U ⋊ K) and λ, λ̃ as in Theorem 2.4.4, for each m ≥ 1: (i) arguing as in [NT16 p. 58], RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m) ≅ RΓ(K̃^S_P × K_S, RΓ(Inf^{P^S×K_S}_{G^S×K_S} 𝔛_G, R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}} 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)), where R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}} sends P^S × K̃_{P,S}-equivariant complexes of sheaves on 𝔛_G to P^S × K_S-equivariant ones; (ii) the K̃_P-equivariant embedding 𝒱_λ → 𝒱_λ̃^{K̃_{U,S}} ⊂ 𝒱_λ̃, which splits K-equivariantly [NT16 Cor. 2.11], makes 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m a direct summand of R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}(𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m): the inclusion is 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m → (𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)^{K̃_{U,S}} → R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m and the retraction is R1_*^{K̃_{U,S}}𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m → 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m (restriction to the trivial subgroup) followed by the splitting 𝒱_λ̃ → 𝒱_λ mod ϖ^m; (iii) hence r_G^* RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m) is a direct summand of RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m) in D(H(P^S × K̃_{P,S}, K̃_P) ⊗_Z O/ϖ^m), and 𝒮 = r_G ∘ r_P descends to (2.4.7) T̃^S(RΓ(X^P_{K̃_P}, 𝒱_λ̃/ϖ^m)) → T̃^S(RΓ(X_K, 𝒱_λ/ϖ^m)).

sourceCoverage.statement: F is a CM field containing an imaginary quadratic field, n ≥ 1, p a prime, E/Q_p inside Q̄_p containing all embeddings of F, and every p-adic place of F⁺ splits in F. sourceCoverage.name: Fontaine–Laffaille categories MF_O, MF^a_O, MF^0_O, MF_k, MF^a_k
sourceCoverage.statement: Standing hypotheses of §4: F is a CM field, p is unramified in F and F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits; E/Q_p contains the images of all embeddings of F; S is a finite set of finite places of F containing the p-adic places, with S = S^c, and for every finite place w ∉ S of F with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic field F_0 ⊂ F. Let v | p be a place of F, so F_v/Q_p is unramified. MF_O is the category of finite O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O-modules M with (i) a decreasing filtration Fil^i M by O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O-submodules that are O_{F_v}-direct summands, such that for each τ: F_v ↪ E, writing M_τ = M ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗O, τ⊗1} O, there is an integer a_τ with Fil^{a_τ} M_τ = M_τ and Fil^{a_τ+p−1} M_τ = 0; and (ii) Frob_p^{−1}⊗1-semilinear maps Φ^i: Fil^i M → M with Φ^i|_{Fil^{i+1} M} = pΦ^{i+1} and M = Σ_i Φ^i(Fil^i M). Then Fil^i M = ∏_τ Fil^i M_τ and Φ^i = ∏_τ Φ^i_τ with Φ^i_τ: Fil^i M_τ → M_{τ∘Frob_p} (printed M_{τ∘Frob_p^{−1}}). For a = (a_τ) ∈ Z^{Hom(F_v,E)}, MF^a_O is the full subcategory of M with Fil^{a_τ} M_τ = M_τ and Fil^{a_τ+p−1} M_τ = 0 for every τ; MF^0_O = MF^{(0,…,0)}_O; MF_k and MF^a_k are the full subcategories of MF_O and MF^a_O of objects killed by ϖ.

sourceCoverage.name: The Fontaine–Laffaille functor G^0 on MF^0_O and its tensor compatibility (4.1.1)
sourceCoverage.statement: For p > 2 there is an exact, fully faithful, covariant functor G^0 from MF^0_O to the category of finite O-modules with continuous O-linear G_{F_v}-action ([CHT08, §2.4.1], where it is called G). Its essential image is closed under subquotients, and on MF^0_k it takes values in continuous G_{F_v}-representations on finite-dimensional k-vector spaces. If M_1, M_2 ∈ MF^0_O and M_1 ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O} M_2 ∈ MF^0_O, then (4.1.1) G^0(M_1 ⊗_{O_{F_v}⊗_{Z_p}O} M_2) = G^0(M_1) ⊗_O G^0(M_2).

sourceCoverage.name: Transfer of the Fontaine–Laffaille property from a flat determinant to a nilpotent quotient (step in Prop. 4.4.6)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let Ã be a finite flat O-algebra, D̃ a continuous 2n-dimensional determinant of G_{F,S} valued in Ã, and M = Ã[G_{F,S}]/ker D̃. Assume the finite O-module M, restricted to each G_{F_v} with v | v̄, lies in the essential image of the integral Fontaine–Laffaille functor G^a in the stated interval. Let Ã → B be an O-algebra homomorphism, where B is a finite Artinian local O-algebra killed by ϖ^m for some m ≥ 1. Suppose D̃_B = det(ρ ⊕ ρ′) for continuous ρ, ρ′: G_{F,S} → GL_n(B), whose residual representations over the residue field of B are absolutely irreducible and non-isomorphic. Then there is a surjection B ⊗_Ã M ↠ B[G_{F,S}]/ker D̃_B, and the latter algebra is isomorphic to M_n(B) × M_n(B). Consequently ρ|_{G_{F_v}} belongs to the essential image of G^a. The coefficient map Ã → B need not be surjective. Kernel inclusion under arbitrary scalar extension, rather than equality under flat scalar extension, gives the displayed surjection; the split matrix-algebra identification requires the residually multiplicity-free reconstruction and faithful determinant argument.

sourceCoverage.name: Setup of §5: the level subgroups K(b,c), the ordinary Hecke algebra T^{S,ord}, U_v and U_p
sourceCoverage.statement: Standing data: F a CM field, n ≥ 1, p a prime, E/Q_p finite containing the images of all embeddings F ↪ Q̄_p; standing hypothesis for all of §5: F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits (p may ramify in F). Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup, λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}, S a finite set of finite places of F containing S_p and stable under c, such that (i) for every finite v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place and l is unramified in F, or l splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (ii) K_v = Iw_v for v | p and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for finite v ∉ S. For integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, K(b,c) ⊂ K is the good subgroup with K(b,c)_v = K_v for v ∤ p and K(b,c)_v = Iw_v(b,c) for v | p; K(0,1) = K and K(0,c)/K(b,c) ≅ ∏_{v|p} T_n(O_{F_v}/ϖ_v^b). Define T^{S,ord} = T^S ⊗_O O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧[{U_{v,1},…,U_{v,n},U_{v,n}^{-1}}_{v|p}] (U_{v,i} formal variables), U_v = U_{v,1}U_{v,2}⋯U_{v,n−1}, U_p = ∏_{v|p} U_v. The canonical surjection O⟦T_n(O_{F,p})⟧ → O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)] extends to T^{S,ord} → End_{D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)])}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)), U_{v,i} acting by the double coset operator [Iw_v(b,c) diag(ϖ_v,…,ϖ_v,1,…,1) Iw_v(b,c)] (i entries ϖ_v). Additional standing hypothesis for §§5.2–5.5: ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c for every v | p; the U_{v,i} depend on ϖ_v but RΓ^ord, T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord and the truth of Theorem 5.5.1 do not.

T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord is the image of T^{S,ord} → End_{D(O[K(0,c)/K(b,c)])}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord), i.e. T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord = T^{S,ord}(RΓ_{K(0,c)/K(b,c)}(X_{K(b,c)}, V_λ)^ord). There is a canonical homomorphism T^S(K(0,c)/K(b,c), V_λ) → T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord (in general neither injective nor surjective); consequently every maximal ideal 𝔪 of T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord has an associated ρ̄_𝔪: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord/𝔪). A maximal ideal of T^{S,ord} with residue field finite over k is of Galois type (resp. non-Eisenstein) if its pullback to T^S is so in the sense of Definition 2.3.6.

sourceCoverage.name: The characters χ_{λ,v,i}
sourceCoverage.statement: The operators U_{v,i} are invertible in T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord (because U_p is). sourceCoverage.name: Theorem 5.5.1: local–global compatibility at l = p, ordinary case
sourceCoverage.statement: Assume the §5 standing hypotheses (F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which p splits; ϖ_{v^c} = ϖ_v^c) and [F^+:Q] > 1. Let K ⊂ GL_n(A_F^∞) be a good subgroup with K_v = Iw_v for each v ∈ S_p (and K_v = GL_n(O_{F_v}) for v ∉ S), let c ≥ b ≥ 0 be integers with c ≥ 1, let λ be a weight (printed λ ∈ (Z^n)^{Hom(F,E)}; the objects require λ ∈ (Z^n_+)^{Hom(F,E)}), and let 𝔪 ⊂ T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Suppose (1) for every finite place v ∉ S with residue characteristic l, either S contains no l-adic place of F and l is unramified in F, or there is an imaginary quadratic F_0 ⊂ F in which l splits; (2) ρ̄_𝔪 is decomposed generic. Then there exist an integer N ≥ 1 depending only on [F^+:Q] and n, an ideal J ⊂ T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord_𝔪 with J^N = 0, and a continuous ρ_𝔪: G_{F,S} → GL_n(T^S(K(b,c),λ)^ord_𝔪/J) such that: (a) for every finite v ∉ S, det(X − ρ_𝔪(Frob_v)) is the image of P_v(X); (b) for every v ∈ S_p and g ∈ G_{F_v}, det(X − ρ_𝔪(g)) = ∏_{i=1}^n (X − χ_{λ,v,i}(g)); (c) for every v ∈ S_p and g_1,…,g_n ∈ G_{F_v}, (ρ_𝔪(g_1) − χ_{λ,v,1}(g_1))(ρ_𝔪(g_2) − χ_{λ,v,2}(g_2))⋯(ρ_𝔪(g_n) − χ_{λ,v,n}(g_n)) = 0.

sourceCoverage.name: Smooth modules over a monoid (§5.2.1, (5.2.2)–(5.2.3))
sourceCoverage.statement: Fix m ≥ 1 and work with O/ϖ^m-coefficients. For a locally profinite group G, Mod(O/ϖ^m[G]) is the category of O/ϖ^m[G]-modules and Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[G]) ⊂ Mod(O/ϖ^m[G]) the full subcategory of smooth modules (5.2.2). For an open submonoid Δ ⊂ G containing an open compact subgroup of G, Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) ⊂ Mod(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) (5.2.3) is the full subcategory of modules in which every vector is fixed by an open subgroup of Δ; M ↦ M^sm (smooth vectors) is right adjoint to the inclusion (5.2.3). D_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) denotes the derived category of Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]).

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 5.2.4: smooth modules over a monoid have enough injectives; restriction preserves injectives
sourceCoverage.statement: Let Δ ⊂ G be an open submonoid of a locally profinite group containing an open compact subgroup. (1) Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) is abelian and has enough injectives. (2) If Δ' ⊂ Δ is a subgroup which is either compact or open (hence locally profinite), the forgetful functor Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ]) → Mod_sm(O/ϖ^m[Δ']) preserves injectives.

sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, c ∈ Aut(F) complex conjugation, p a prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with: (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline for every v | p, and p unramified in F; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1), and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous (Definition 6.2.29); (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n²; (5) there is a cuspidal automorphic π of GL_n(𝔸_F) with (a) π regular algebraic of weight λ satisfying λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for all τ; (b) an isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ with ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π) and HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, λ_{ιτ,2} + n − 2, …, λ_{ιτ,n}} for every τ : F ↪ ℚ̄_p; (c) π_v unramified for every v | p. (Remark 6.1.4, folded here: the image of Pρ̄ equals that of ad ρ̄, so the first half of (4) is equivalent to ζ_p ∉ F̄^{ker ad ρ̄}; when p is unramified in F it follows from the non-existence of a surjection (ad ρ̄)(G_F) ↠ (ℤ/pℤ)^×.)

sourceCoverage.name: Theorem 6.1.2: ordinary automorphy lifting
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, c complex conjugation, p a prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with: (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) for every v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weights: there is λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,ℚ̄_p)} such that for each v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1}, …, ψ_{v,n} : G_{F_v} → ℚ̄_p^×, where ψ_{v,i} agrees on an open subgroup of I_{F_v} with σ ↦ ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(F_v, ℚ̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1)}; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous; (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n; (5) there are a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ with π ι-ordinary and r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄. Then ρ is ordinarily automorphic of weight ιλ: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for an ι-ordinary cuspidal automorphic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight ιλ; for finite v ∤ p with ρ and π unramified at v, Π_v is unramified. (Remark 6.1.3, folded here: the existence of Π forces λ to be conjugate self-dual up to twist, λ_{τ,i} + λ_{τc,n+1−i} = w for some w ∈ ℤ, by Clozel's purity lemma [Clo90, Lem. 4.9]; this is not assumed. The proof shows ρ contributes to the ordinary part of completed cohomology and gets Π by 'independence of weight'.)

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 6.2.19: lifts at a Taylor–Wiles place split as sums of characters
sourceCoverage.statement: Assume q_v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} unramified, Λ_v = 𝒪, and ρ̄(Frob_v) has n distinct eigenvalues α_1, …, α_n ∈ k; let γ̄_i : G_{F_v} → k^× be unramified with γ̄_i(Frob_v) = α_i. For any lift ρ : G_{F_v} → GL_n(A) of ρ̄|_{G_{F_v}} there are unique continuous characters γ_i : G_{F_v} → A^× with γ_i mod 𝔪_A = γ̄_i such that ρ is GL_n(A)-conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ γ_n.

sourceCoverage.name: The diamond group Δ_v and the map 𝒪[Δ_v] → R_v^□ at a Taylor–Wiles place
sourceCoverage.statement: Let Δ_v = k(v)^×(p)^n, k(v)^×(p) the maximal p-power quotient of k(v)^×. Writing the universal lift over R_v^□ as conjugate to γ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ γ_n (Lemma 6.2.19), each γ_i ∘ Art_{F_v}|_{𝒪_{F_v}^×} factors through k(v)^×(p), giving a canonical local 𝒪-algebra map 𝒪[Δ_v] → R_v^□ (depending on the ordering α_1, …, α_n). sourceCoverage.name: Taylor–Wiles data, the augmented problem 𝒮_Q and the Λ[Δ_Q]-structure
sourceCoverage.statement: Assume k contains all eigenvalues of elements of ρ̄(G_F). sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 6.2.32: existence of Taylor–Wiles data killing the dual Selmer group

sourceCoverage.name: The abstract Ihara-avoidance set-up (§6.3.5)
sourceCoverage.statement: Λ is a power series ring over 𝒪, and one is given: (1) S_∞ = Λ⟦X_1, …, X_r⟧ with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞ = (X_1, …, X_r); (2) perfect complexes C_∞, C′_∞ of S_∞-modules and a fixed isomorphism C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/ϖ ≅ C′_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/ϖ in D(S_∞/ϖ); (3) S_∞-subalgebras T_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(C_∞) and T′_∞ ⊂ End_{D(S_∞)}(C′_∞) with the same image T̄_∞ in End_{D(S_∞/ϖ)}(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ) = End_{D(S_∞/ϖ)}(C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ) (T_∞, T′_∞ are then finite over S_∞); (4) Noetherian complete local S_∞-algebras R_∞, R′_∞ with surjections R_∞ ↠ T_∞/I_∞, R′_∞ ↠ T′_∞/I′_∞, I_∞, I′_∞ nilpotent, with images Ī_∞, Ī′_∞ in T̄_∞ (so supports of H^*(C_∞), H^*(C′_∞) over R_∞, R′_∞ make sense and lie in Spec T_∞, Spec T′_∞, finite over Spec S_∞); (5) an isomorphism R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ compatible with the S_∞-algebra structures and with the actions on H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞) = H^*(C′_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/ϖ)/(Ī_∞ + Ī′_∞); (6) integers q_0 ∈ ℤ, l_0 ∈ ℤ_{≥0}.

sourceCoverage.name: Assumption 6.3.6: dimension, component and generic-concentration hypotheses
sourceCoverage.statement: (1) dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = dim S_∞ − l_0 and dim R_∞/ϖ = dim R′_∞/ϖ = dim S_∞ − l_0 − 1. (2) Each generic point of Spec R_∞/ϖ of maximal dimension (dim R_∞ − 1) is the specialization of a unique generic point of Spec R_∞ of dimension dim R_∞; Spec R′_∞ has a unique generic point x′ of dimension dim R_∞; generic points of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞, Spec R_∞/ϖ not of maximal dimension have dimension < dim S_∞ − l_0 − 1 (so the maximal-dimensional generic points of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞ have characteristic 0). (3) There is a one-dimensional characteristic-0 prime 𝔭 ⊃ 𝔞_∞ of S_∞ with H^*(C_∞ ⊗^L_{S_∞} S_∞/𝔭)[1/p] ≠ 0 and nonzero only in degrees [q_0, q_0 + l_0]. sourceCoverage.name: Corollary 6.3.9: support after specialization at a characteristic-0 point

sourceCoverage.name: Ultrapatching set-up: the patching datum (fixed ultrafilter, S_∞, R_∞ and the finite-level systems)
sourceCoverage.statement: Fix a non-principal ultrafilter 𝔉 on ℕ = {N ≥ 1} and a ring Λ isomorphic to a power series ring over 𝒪. Let δ, g, q be positive integers, Δ_∞ = ℤ_p^{nq}, 𝒯 a formal power series ring over Λ (framing variables) and S_∞ = 𝒯⟦Δ_∞⟧, an augmented Λ-algebra with augmentation ideal 𝔞_∞. Let R^loc, R′^loc ∈ CNL_Λ with a fixed isomorphism R^loc/ϖ ≅ R′^loc/ϖ, and let R_∞, R′_∞ be the power series rings in g variables over R^loc, R′^loc. Level-0 compatibility (N ≥ 1): isomorphisms π_N: 𝒞_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ 𝒞_0 and π′_N: 𝒞′_N ⊗^L_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ 𝒞′_0 in D(Λ), compatible mod ϖ, such that the induced maps T_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → End_{D(Λ)}(𝒞_0) (resp. primed) factor through maps T_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → T_0 (resp. T′_N ⊗ Λ → T′_0) that become surjective after composing with T_0 → T_0/I_0 (resp. T′_0 → T′_0/I′_0); and isomorphisms R_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ R_0, R′_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ ≅ R′_0, compatible mod ϖ and with the maps from R_∞, R′_∞ in (4), under which, writing I_{N,0}, I′_{N,0} for the images of I_N, I′_N in T_0/I_0, T′_0/I′_0, the surjections R_N ⊗_{Λ[Δ_N]} Λ → (T_0/I_0)/I_{N,0} and R′_N ⊗ Λ → (T′_0/I′_0)/I′_{N,0} coincide with the maps R_0 → (T_0/I_0)/I_{N,0} and R′_0 → (T′_0/I′_0)/I′_{N,0}.

sourceCoverage.name: §6.5.1: standing data and hypotheses (1)–(17) for the Fontaine–Laffaille patching argument; the level K
sourceCoverage.statement: F is an imaginary CM field and we fix: (1) an integer n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n²; (2) a finite set S of finite places of F containing S_p; (3) a possibly empty subset R ⊂ S of places prime to p; (4) a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight λ; (5) an isomorphism ι: Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Assume: (6) every prime l lying below a place of S, or ramified in F, splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F (so each place of S is split over F⁺ and F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified); (7) p is unramified in F; (8) λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for every τ: F ↪ ℂ; (9) for each v ∈ S_p, with v̄ = v|_{F⁺}, there is a place v̄′ ≠ v̄ of F⁺ above p with Σ_{v̄″ ≠ v̄, v̄′} [F⁺_{v̄″}:ℚ_p] > ½[F⁺:ℚ]; (10) r̄_ι(π) is absolutely irreducible; (11) π_v is unramified for v | p; (12) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (13) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v is unramified, v ∉ R^c and H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (14) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (15) π_v is unramified at every finite v ∉ S; (16) for v ∈ R: q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial; (17) r̄_ι(π) is decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1) and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has enormous image (Definition 6.2.29). The level K = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GL_n(Ô_F): K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for v ∉ S or v ∈ S_p; K_v = Iw_v for v ∈ R; K_v = Iw_{v,1} (pro-v Iwahori) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p).

sourceCoverage.name: Corollary 6.5.5: automorphy lifting under the §6.5.1 hypotheses
sourceCoverage.statement: Under (1)–(17) of §6.5.1, let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous with: (1) ρ̄ ≅ r̄_ι(π); (2) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} crystalline for every v | p, with HT_τ(ρ) = {λ_{ιτ,1} + n − 1, …, λ_{ιτ,n}} (the j-th entry λ_{ιτ,j} + n − j) for every τ: F ↪ Q̄_p; (3) ρ unramified at every finite v ∉ S; (4) ρ|_{G_{F_v}} unipotently ramified for v ∈ R. sourceCoverage.name: Auxiliary Taylor–Wiles levels K_1(Q) ⊂ K_0(Q) ⊂ K and the Hecke algebra maps (6.5.6), (6.5.7)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let (Q, (α_{v,1},…,α_{v,n})_{v∈Q}) be a Taylor–Wiles datum for 𝒮_1 (§6.2.28) such that for each v ∈ Q the residue characteristic l_v splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F. It is a Taylor–Wiles datum for every 𝒮_χ, and R_{𝒮_{χ,Q}} is an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra, Δ_Q = ∏_{v∈Q} Δ_v = ∏_{v∈Q} k(v)^×(p)^n. sourceCoverage.name: Very weakly and extremely weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a number field. A rank n very weakly compatible system R of l-adic representations of G_F defined over M is a 5-tuple (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) with: (1) M a number field; (2) S a finite set of primes of F; (3) for each prime v ∉ S of F, Q_v(X) ∈ M[X] monic of degree n; (4) for each τ : F ↪ M̄, H_τ a multiset of n integers; (5) for each prime λ of M, of residue characteristic l, a continuous semisimple r_λ : G_F → GL_n(M̄_λ) such that (a) if v ∉ S and v ∤ l then r_λ is unramified at v and r_λ(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial Q_v(X); (b) for l outside a set of rational primes of Dirichlet density 0, r_λ|_{G_{F_v}} is crystalline for all v | l and HT_τ(r_λ) = H_τ for every M̄ ↪ M̄_λ over M; (c) for all λ, HT_τ(det r_λ) = Σ_{h∈H_τ} h. Dropping (5b) gives an extremely weakly compatible system (it depends on the H_τ only through (5c)). Conventions: Frob_v is a geometric Frobenius and HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1}. (Used implicitly: every compatible family of characters is de Rham, by Henniart.)

sourceCoverage.name: Regular, irreducible and strongly irreducible compatible systems
sourceCoverage.statement: A very or extremely weakly compatible system R (as in BLGGT §5.1, mutatis mutandis) is regular if every H_τ consists of n distinct integers; irreducible if there is a set 𝓛 of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that r_λ is irreducible for all λ | l ∈ 𝓛; strongly irreducible if R|_{G_{F'}} is irreducible for every finite extension F'/F.

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 7.1.1: rank-2 systems are irreducible at every λ or split as a sum of compatible characters
sourceCoverage.statement: If R is an extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2, then either r_λ is irreducible for every λ, or there are weakly compatible systems (in the sense of BLGGT) 𝒳_1, 𝒳_2 of rank 1 with r_λ ≅ χ_{1,λ} ⊕ χ_{2,λ} for every λ.

sourceCoverage.name: Reducible and Artin-up-to-twist rank-2 systems
sourceCoverage.statement: An extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2 is reducible if it is not irreducible; by Lemma 7.1.1 every r_λ is then reducible. A very (or extremely) weakly compatible system of rank 2 is Artin up to twist if, after possibly enlarging M, there are an irreducible Artin representation ρ : G_F → GL_2(M̄) with traces in M and a weakly compatible system of characters χ_λ with r_λ ≅ ρ ⊗ χ_λ for all λ.

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 7.1.2: trichotomy for irreducible rank-2 systems (strongly irreducible, Artin up to twist, or induced)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let R be an irreducible extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2. Then either (1) R is strongly irreducible; or (2) R is Artin up to twist; or (3) there are a quadratic extension F'/F and a weakly compatible system 𝒳 of characters of G_{F'} with R ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F} 𝒳 (R is then called induced).

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 7.1.3: residual irreducibility and large residual image for irreducible rank-2 systems
sourceCoverage.statement: Let R be an irreducible extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2. Then for all rational primes l in a set of Dirichlet density 1 and all λ | l, r̄_λ is absolutely irreducible. If moreover R is neither induced nor Artin up to twist, and F̃ is the normal closure of F/Q, then l can in addition be taken so that r̄_λ(G_{F̃}) ⊇ SL_2(F_l) for all λ | l.

sourceCoverage.name: Unramified connected subgroups of products of Res PGL_2 (facts (1)–(8) in the proof of Lemma 7.1.3)
sourceCoverage.statement: Over Q̄_l: (1) every morphism PGL_2 → PGL_2 is trivial or conjugation by an element of PGL_2(Q̄_l); (2) every morphism PGL_2^r → PGL_2 is trivial or a projection followed by a conjugation; (3) up to PGL_2(Q̄_l)^J-conjugacy, morphisms PGL_2^I → PGL_2^J are induced by pairs (J_0 ⊂ J, φ : J_0 → I); (4) Aut(PGL_2^I) = PGL_2^I ⋊ S_I; (5) a connected algebraic subgroup G ⊂ PGL_2^J surjecting onto PGL_2 under every projection is ≅ PGL_2^I, embedded (up to conjugacy) through a surjection φ : J ↠ I (induction on #J and Goursat); (6) for M/Q_l finite, (Res^M_{Q_l} PGL_2)_{Q̄_l} ≅ PGL_2^{Hom_{Q_l}(M,Q̄_l)} with G_{Q_l} acting through its left action on Hom_{Q_l}(M, Q̄_l); (7) forms of PGL_2^r are classified by the middle term of H^1(Q_l, PGL_2^r) → H^1(Q_l, Aut PGL_2^r) → H^1(Q_l, S_r), and the unramified ones (quasi-split and split over an unramified extension) are exactly ∏_i Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2 with N_i/Q_l unramified; (8) hence, if G ⊂ ∏_{j∈J} Res^{M_j}_{Q_l} PGL_2 is an unramified connected subgroup whose base change to Q̄_l surjects onto every factor of PGL_2^{⊔_j Hom(M_j,Q̄_l)}, then G ≅ ∏_{i∈I} Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2 with N_i/Q_l unramified, and each (j, τ)-projection of G_{Q̄_l} is PGL_2(Q̄_l)-conjugate to the projection onto one factor of ∏_i (Res^{N_i}_{Q_l} PGL_2)_{Q̄_l}.

sourceCoverage.name: Pure compatible systems
sourceCoverage.statement: A very or extremely weakly compatible system R is pure of weight w if (i) for each v ∉ S, each root α ∈ M̄ of Q_v(X) and each ı : M̄ ↪ C, |ıα|² = q_v^w; and (ii) for each τ : F ↪ M̄ and each complex conjugation c ∈ Gal(M̄/Q), H_{cτ} = {w − h : h ∈ H_τ}.

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 7.1.9: under (DGI), R_π is very weakly compatible

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 7.1.10: for GL_2, R_π is irreducible, satisfies (DGI) and is very weakly compatible

sourceCoverage.name: Ordinarily automorphic representations (residual and l-adic)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let E be a CM or totally real field, l a prime and ι: Q̄_l ≅ C the fixed isomorphism. A residual representation r̄: G_E → GL_n(F̄_l) is ι-ordinarily automorphic if it has an automorphic lift r ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) (Definition 1.3) such that π is ι-ordinary at every place v | l, in the sense of Geraghty [8, Definition 5.3]. This is a condition on the eigenvalues of the normalized Hecke operators on π_v, not on r|G_{E_v}. Applied to an l-adic representation r: G_E → GL_n(Q̄_l), the same term means that r ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) for a regular algebraic cuspidal π that is ι-ordinary at every v | l. The paper uses it in this sense in Lemma 4.3 and in the conclusion of Theorem 1.4 without defining it separately, and it is the form of the conclusion of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. Ordinarity of r_{l,ι}(π)|G_{E_v} for v | l does not replace this condition. As Remark 4.4 explains, the local–global compatibility that would deduce automorphic ordinarity from it assumes polarizability.

sourceCoverage.name: Decomposed genericity of symmetric powers under avoidance
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F/Q be a finite extension with normal closure F̃, n a positive integer, l > 2n + 5 a prime, and r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) a continuous representation with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). Put H = F̃ · F̄^{ker ad r̄}, and let H′ be the normal closure of H over Q. Let F_1/F be a finite Galois extension that is linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F and linearly disjoint from H′ over F. Then Sym^{n−1} r̄|_{G_{F_1}} is decomposed generic. For n = 1 this is immediate, since Sym^0 r̄ is the trivial character; for n ≥ 2 the proof rests on ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3) with m = n − 1.
sourceCoverage.locator: Lemma 2.6(2), p. 1251; proof pp. 1251–1252; NSF online-first PDF pp. 13–14 (journal pagination inferred from 1239–1275)

sourceCoverage.name: Ordinary automorphy lifting theorem over CM and totally real fields (ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM or totally real field, c complex conjugation, p a prime, and ρ : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) continuous with: (1) ρ unramified almost everywhere; (2) for every v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge–Tate weights: there is λ ∈ (ℤ^n_+)^{Hom(F,ℚ̄_p)} such that for each v | p, ρ|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ an upper-triangular representation with diagonal characters ψ_{v,1}, …, ψ_{v,n} : G_{F_v} → ℚ̄_p^×, where ψ_{v,i} agrees on an open subgroup of I_{F_v} with σ ↦ ∏_{τ ∈ Hom(F_v, ℚ̄_p)} τ(Art_{F_v}^{-1}(σ))^{−(λ_{τ,n−i+1} + i − 1)}; (3) ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic, and ρ̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) enormous; (4) there is σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_p)} with ρ̄(σ) scalar, and p > n; (5) there are a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ with π ι-ordinary and r̄_ι(π) ≅ ρ̄. Then ρ is ordinarily automorphic of weight ιλ: ρ ≅ r_ι(Π) for an ι-ordinary cuspidal automorphic Π of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight ιλ; for finite v ∤ p with ρ and π unramified at v, Π_v is unramified. (Remark 6.1.3, folded here: the existence of Π forces λ to be conjugate self-dual up to twist, λ_{τ,i} + λ_{τc,n+1−i} = w for some w ∈ ℤ, by Clozel's purity lemma [Clo90, Lem. 4.9]; this is not assumed. The proof shows ρ contributes to the ordinary part of completed cohomology and gets Π by 'independence of weight'.)
sourceCoverage.locator: ACC+ (Allen et al., Ann. of Math. 197 (2023)), Theorem 6.1.2, pp. 1029–1030; applied in the proofs of Theorem 1.1 (pp. 1272–1273) and Theorem 1.4 (p. 1274)

sourceCoverage.name: Preservation of decomposed genericity in the final base change
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a number field and r̄: G_F → GL_n(F̄_l) continuous, absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. Let K/Q be a Galois extension linearly disjoint over Q from the Galois closure over Q of F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Then r̄|G_{FK} is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. In the proof of Theorem 1.4 this is applied with K = L′LF^suff(ζ_N), which is Galois over Q with K ∩ F^avoid = Q, and FK = F′. The paper asserts the disjointness for F′ itself, which is impossible because both fields contain F (correction E3).
sourceCoverage.locator: ACC+ (Allen et al., Ann. of Math. 197 (2023)), Lemma 7.1.7, p. 1091; applied in the proof of Theorem 1.4 (last paragraph of §4), p. 1274, with correction E3

sourceCoverage.name: Linearly disjoint restriction preserves the residual image and the lifting hypotheses
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a number field, l a prime, r: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) continuous with residual representation r̄, and M = F^{ker r̄}(ζ_l). Let F'/F be a finite extension linearly disjoint from M over F. Then G_{F'} surjects onto Gal(M/F), so r̄(G_{F'}) = r̄(G_F) and r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) = r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}). Consequently: r̄|G_{F'} is absolutely irreducible if r̄ is; r̄(G_{F'(ζ_l)}) is enormous if r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) is; and if σ ∈ G_F − G_{F(ζ_l)} has r̄(σ) scalar, then some σ' ∈ G_{F'} − G_{F'(ζ_l)} has r̄(σ') = r̄(σ). If r is unramified almost everywhere, so is r|G_{F'}. Suppose r|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable and ordinary of weight λ_v (Definition 1.2). Then for each place w | v of F', r|G_{F'_w} is potentially semistable and ordinary of weight (λ_{v,τ'|F_v})_{τ'}, by the compatibility Art_{F_v} ∘ N_{F'_w/F_v} = (restriction) ∘ Art_{F'_w}. Decomposed genericity is not covered here; it needs ACC+ Lemma 7.1.7.
sourceCoverage.locator: Remark after Definition 1.3, p. 1241; proof of Theorem 1.4, p. 1274 ('all conditions except decomposed genericity follows from the corresponding conditions of r̄'); NSF online-first PDF pp. 3 and 36

sourceCoverage.name: Decomposed genericity of Sym^m r̄ when the adjoint image over the Galois closure is large (ACC+ Lemma 7.1.6(3))
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F/Q be finite with normal closure F̃, m a positive integer, l > 2m + 3 a prime, and r̄: G_F → GL_2(F̄_l) continuous with r̄(G_{F̃}) ⊃ SL_2(F_l). Let F′/F be a finite extension linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄} over F, with normal closure F̃′ over Q. If ad r̄(G_{F̃′}) ⊃ PSL_2(F_l), then Sym^m r̄|_{G_{F′}} is decomposed generic.
sourceCoverage.locator: Allen–Calegari–Caraiani–Gee–Helm–Le Hung–Newton–Scholze–Taylor–Thorne, Potential automorphy over CM fields, Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), Lemma 7.1.6(3), pp. 1090–1091; used in the proof of Lemma 2.6(2), p. 1251

sourceCoverage.name: Composita of Galois extensions with a common simple group
sourceCoverage.statement: Let k be a field, Δ a finite simple group, and K_1, …, K_s finite Galois extensions of k inside a common field, each equal to k or with Galois group isomorphic to Δ. Then there is a subset J ⊂ {1, …, s} such that the compositum K = K_1⋯K_s is the compositum of the K_j with j ∈ J, and restriction identifies Gal(K/k) with ∏_{j∈J} Gal(K_j/k) ≅ Δ^{|J|}. In particular, for disjoint subsets I, I′ of J, the composita of the K_j over j ∈ I and over j ∈ I′ are linearly disjoint over k.
sourceCoverage.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.6(2), pp. 1251–1252 (the claims 'Gal(Ẽ/E) = (Z/2Z)^r' and 'Gal(F̃′_i/F̃′_{i−1}) … is of form Δ_i^m', both attributed to Goursat's lemma); NSF online-first PDF pp. 13–14 (journal pagination inferred from 1239–1275)

sourceCoverage.name: ι-ordinary automorphic representation (Geraghty, Definition 5.3)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a CM or totally real field, π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight λ, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and v | l a place of F with uniformizer ϖ_v. For integers c ≥ b ≥ 0, let Iw_v(b,c) ⊂ GL_n(O_{F_v}) be the subgroup of matrices that are upper triangular modulo ϖ_v^c and unipotent upper triangular modulo ϖ_v^b. π is ι-ordinary at v if, for some integers c ≥ b ≥ 0 with c ≥ 1, the Iw_v(b,c)-invariants of ι^{−1}π_v contain a nonzero vector with the following property: for each j = 1, …, n, it is an eigenvector of the weight-normalized Hecke operator U^{(j)}_{λ,ϖ_v} attached to α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) (with j entries ϖ_v), with an l-adic unit eigenvalue. π is ι-ordinary if this holds at every v | l.
sourceCoverage.locator: Geraghty, Math. Ann. 373 (2019), Definition 5.3 (reference [8]); cited in Definition 1.3, p. 1241; used in Lemma 4.3, p. 1273, and in ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(5) (p. 1030) and Corollary 5.5.2 (p. 1028); the groups Iw_v(b,c) as recalled in ACC+, p. 922

sourceCoverage.name: Ordinarity criterion for a twisted Steinberg component (Geraghty, Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6, as used in Lemma 4.3)
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be a CM field, l a prime, ι: Q̄_l ≅ C, and v | l a place of F with uniformizer ϖ_v. Use geometric Artin reciprocity and HT(ε_l) = {−1}. Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) of weight λ in the ACC+ convention, with λ_{τ,i} = c_τ for all i = 1, …, n and all τ: F_v → Q̄_l; thus HT_τ(r_{l,ι}(π)) = {c_τ, c_τ + 1, …, c_τ + n − 1}. Suppose π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|_v^{(1−n)/2}) with ψ_v an unramified character of F_v^×. Suppose also that val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v})) = val_l(∏_{τ:F_v → Q̄_l} τ(ϖ_v)^{+jc_τ}) for every integer 0 ≤ j ≤ n, where α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = diag(ϖ_v, …, ϖ_v, 1, …, 1) with j entries ϖ_v. Then π is ι-ordinary at v. Since det α^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = ϖ_v^j, the condition for j = n implies it for every j. This is the corrected general-weight form of the criterion used in Qian's proof of Lemma 4.3 (E43). In items 087–088 substitute c_τ = λ_τ, the first Hodge–Tate weight, without changing its sign. Geraghty's Lemma 5.6 treats weight 0; Qian checks the central-character valuation to apply the criterion in general weight.
sourceCoverage.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.3, second paragraph, p. 1273, citing Lemmas 5.2 and 5.6 of Geraghty [8]

sourceCoverage.name: Definition 6.1.1: very weakly compatible systems, restriction and tensor product
sourceCoverage.statement: A very weakly compatible system R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_λ}, {H_τ}) of rank n [ACC+ §7]: M a number field, S a finite set of finite places, monic degree-n Q_v(X) ∈ M[X] for v ∉ S, multisets H_τ for τ : F ↪ M̄, and continuous semisimple r_λ : G_F → GL_n(M̄_λ) with (a) r_λ unramified at v ∉ S, v ∤ l, with char r_λ(Frob_v) = Q_v(X); (b) for l outside a density-0 set, r_λ crystalline with HT_τ = H_τ; (c) HT_τ(det r_λ) = Σ_{h∈H_τ} h. Restriction to F′/F and tensor products over a common M are defined.

sourceCoverage.name: Definition 6.1.2 (1), (2), (4), (5): pure, automorphic, irreducible and strongly irreducible systems
sourceCoverage.statement: R is pure of weight m if |ια|² = q_v^m for the roots of Q_v and H_{cτ} = {m − h : h ∈ H_τ}; automorphic if some regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : M ↪ ℂ give π_v unramified with rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) of characteristic polynomial ι(Q_v(X)) for all v ∉ S; irreducible if r_λ is irreducible for l outside a density-0 set; strongly irreducible if R|_{G_{F′}} is irreducible for every finite F′/F.

sourceCoverage.name: Definition 6.1.2 (3): weakly automorphic of level prime to T
sourceCoverage.statement: For T a finite set of finite places disjoint from S, R is weakly automorphic of level prime to T if there are a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F) and ι : M ↪ ℂ such that for all but finitely many v ∉ S and for every v ∈ T, π_v is unramified and rec^T_{F_v}(π_v)(Frob_v) has characteristic polynomial ι(Q_v(X)); weakly automorphic means T = ∅.

sourceCoverage.name: The compatible system of a regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2 over a CM field
sourceCoverage.statement: For F CM and π regular algebraic cuspidal of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight λ there is an associated automorphic very weakly compatible system R = (M, S, {Q_v(X)}, {r_{π,λ}}, {H_τ}) with H_τ = {λ_{τ,1} + 1, λ_{τ,2}} [ACC+ Lem. 7.1.10].

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 6.1.4: weakly automorphic and pure implies automorphic
sourceCoverage.statement: Let F be CM and R a very weakly compatible system of rank n that is weakly automorphic, via π, and pure of weight m. Then R is automorphic.

sourceCoverage.name: Lemma 6.1.5: primes of large image have density one
sourceCoverage.statement: Let R be a strongly irreducible very weakly compatible system of rank 2 over a number field F. The set L(R) of primes l not lying below any place of S such that r_λ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights H_τ and r̄_λ(G_{F̃}) contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_l) for every λ | l (F̃ the Galois closure of F/ℚ) has Dirichlet density 1.

sourceCoverage.name: The trichotomy for rank-2 compatible systems
sourceCoverage.statement: Let R be an irreducible extremely weakly compatible system of rank 2. Then either (1) R is strongly irreducible; or (2) R is Artin up to twist; or (3) there are a quadratic extension F'/F and a weakly compatible system 𝒳 of characters of G_{F'} with R ≅ Ind_{G_{F'}}^{G_F} 𝒳 (R is then called induced).
sourceCoverage.locator: §7.1, proof of Theorem 7.1.1, p. 61; proof of Theorem 7.2.1, pp. 61–62

sourceCoverage.name: Symmetric powers of very weakly compatible systems
sourceCoverage.statement: For a very weakly compatible system R of rank 2 with H_τ = {0, m}, Sym^{n−1}R has representations Sym^{n−1}r_λ, weights {0, m, …, (n − 1)m} and determinant det^{n(n−1)/2}. Here n≥1. Regularity follows when m≠0; for m=0 and n>1 the Hodge multiset has repetitions. No automorphy or purity is inferred from the operation alone.

sourceCoverage.name: Proposition 6.5.13(1): soluble base change for regular algebraic cuspidal representations
sourceCoverage.statement: Fix n ≥ 2, a prime p and ι: Q̄_p → ℂ. Let F be imaginary CM or totally real and E/F a finite Galois extension with Gal(E/F) soluble and E imaginary CM or totally real. Let π be a cuspidal regular algebraic automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ = (λ_τ)_{τ∈Hom(F,ℂ)} with r_ι(π)|_{G_E} irreducible. Then there is a cuspidal regular algebraic π_E of GL_n(𝔸_E) of weight λ_{E,τ} = λ_{τ|_F} (τ ∈ Hom(E,ℂ); printed λ_{τ|E}) with r_ι(π_E) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E}, and rec_{E_w}(π_E) = rec_{F_v}(π)|_{W_{E_w}} for every finite place w | v. (Proof: induct to E/F cyclic of prime order with generator σ and nontrivial η: Gal(E/F) → ℂ^×; π ⊗ (η ∘ Art_F^{-1}) ≇ π since otherwise r_ι(π)|_{G_E} would be reducible; [AC89, Ch. 3, Thms 4.2, 5.1] give Π cuspidal of weight λ_E with Π_w a lift of π_{w|F} at almost all w, and Chebotarev gives r_ι(Π) ≅ r_ι(π)|_{G_E}.)

sourceCoverage.name: Proposition 6.5.13(2): soluble descent of automorphy
sourceCoverage.statement: Same F, E, n, p, ι. Let ρ: G_F → GL_n(Q̄_p) be continuous with ρ|_{G_E} irreducible, and suppose ρ|_{G_E} ≅ r_ι(π) for a cuspidal regular algebraic π of GL_n(𝔸_E) of weight λ. Define λ_F by λ_{F,τ} = λ_{τ′} for any extension τ′: E ↪ ℂ of τ: F ↪ ℂ; λ_F is independent of choices, and there is a cuspidal regular algebraic π_F of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ_F with ρ ≅ r_ι(π_F), and rec_{E_w}(π) = rec_{F_v}(π_F)|_{W_{E_w}} for every finite w | v (printed without the restriction). (Proof: for E/F cyclic of prime order, strong multiplicity one gives π^σ ≅ π; [AC89, Ch. 3, Thms 4.2, 5.1] give Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight λ_F with π_w a lift of Π_{w|F} at almost all w; Chebotarev gives r_ι(Π)|_{G_E} ≅ ρ|_{G_E}, and irreducibility of ρ|_{G_E} gives π_F = Π ⊗ (η ∘ Art_F^{-1})^i with r_ι(π_F) ≅ ρ.)

contexts.conventions: Frobenius and Artin reciprocity are geometric; HT(ε)={−1}. Dominant GL_n rows are descending; HT_τ(V_λ)={λ_{τ,i}+n−i}. O is the ring of integers of a finite p-adic E containing all embeddings, varpi its uniformizer and k its residue field. d=n²[F⁺:Q], dim X_K=d−1. The choice of lifts above p identifies the split unitary rank-2n factors with GL_{2n}. Non-neat levels use the arithmetic groupoid; a finite free cellular model is invoked only after stabilizers are trivial or the indicated invertibility condition is proved. For rational GL_n cohomology put f=[F⁺:Q], q_GL=n(n−1)f/2 and ℓ₀=nf−1. The dual arithmetic complex is RHom(RΓ,O)[−d], so H^i dualizes H^{d−i}. Its rational range is [q_patch,q_patch+ℓ₀], q_patch=q_GL+1, since 2q_GL+ℓ₀=d−1. The q₀ in the abstract patching hypotheses denotes q_patch, not q_GL.
contexts.FL-good-level: F is an imaginary CM field and we fix: (1) an integer n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n²; (2) a finite set S of finite places of F containing S_p; (3) a possibly empty subset R ⊂ S of places prime to p; (4) a cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight λ; (5) an isomorphism ι: Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Assume: (6) every prime l lying below a place of S, or ramified in F, splits in some imaginary quadratic subfield of F (so each place of S is split over F⁺ and F/F⁺ is everywhere unramified); (7) p is unramified in F; (8) λ_{τ,1} + λ_{τc,1} − λ_{τ,n} − λ_{τc,n} < p − 2n for every τ: F ↪ ℂ; (9) for each v ∈ S_p, with v̄ = v|_{F⁺}, there is a place v̄′ ≠ v̄ of F⁺ above p with Σ_{v̄″ ≠ v̄, v̄′} [F⁺_{v̄″}:ℚ_p] > ½[F⁺:ℚ]; (10) r̄_ι(π) is absolutely irreducible; (11) π_v is unramified for v | p; (12) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (13) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v is unramified, v ∉ R^c and H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (14) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (15) π_v is unramified at every finite v ∉ S; (16) for v ∈ R: q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} is trivial; (17) r̄_ι(π) is decomposed generic (Definition 4.3.1) and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has enormous image (Definition 6.2.29). The level K = ∏_v K_v ⊂ GL_n(Ô_F): K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) for v ∉ S or v ∈ S_p; K_v = Iw_v for v ∈ R; K_v = Iw_{v,1} (pro-v Iwahori) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p).
contexts.ordinary-good-level: F is an imaginary CM field and we fix: (1) an integer n ≥ 2 and a prime p > n; (2) a finite set S of finite places containing S_p; (3) a possibly empty R ⊂ S of places prime to p; (4) a cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F), regular algebraic of weight μ; (5) ι: Q̄_p ≅ ℂ. Assume: (6) every prime below a place of S, or ramified in F, splits in an imaginary quadratic subfield of F; (7) r̄_ι(π) absolutely irreducible; (8) for v ∈ S_p, π_v^{Iw_v(1,1)} ≠ 0 and π is ι-ordinary at v ([Ger19, Def. 5.3]); (9) π_v^{Iw_v} ≠ 0 for v ∈ R; (10) for v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p): π_v unramified, v ∉ R^c, H²(F_v, ad r̄_ι(π)) = 0; (11) S − (R ∪ S_p) contains two places of distinct residue characteristics; (12) π_v unramified for finite v ∉ S; (13) for v ∈ R: q_v ≡ 1 mod p and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial; (14) r̄_ι(π) decomposed generic and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} of enormous image; (15) for v ∈ S_p: [F_v:ℚ_p] > n(n+1)/2 + 1 and r̄_ι(π)|_{G_{F_v}} trivial. The level K = ∏ K_v: K_v = GL_n(𝒪_{F_v}) (v ∉ S), Iw_v(1,1) (v ∈ S_p), Iw_v (v ∈ R), Iw_{v,1} (v ∈ S − (R ∪ S_p)); K is neat (Lemma 6.5.2), hence good.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.3, proof of Lemma 4.3.6, criterion (4.3.7), pp. 974–975 (also in arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.reason: Since λ^∨_{σ,i} = −λ_{σ,n+1−i} (§2.2.1), a w violating CTG (Definition 4.3.5) has λ_{w,σ,i} + λ_{w,σc,n+1−i} = i_0 for all σ and i, hence Σ_i(λ_{w,σ,i} + λ_{w,σc,i}) = n·i_0 for every σ, so the '+' inequality implies CTG. With '−', the dictionary (2.2.2) makes Σ_i(μ_{w,τ̃,i} − μ_{w,τ̃c,i}) the sum of all 2n entries of w(μ̃_τ + ρ_τ) − ρ_τ, i.e. of μ̃_τ, for every w, and the printed criterion is false: for n = 1, [F⁺ : Q] = 2, μ̃_{τ_0} = (1, 1), μ̃_τ = (0, 0) it holds for all w (2 ≠ 0), but for w = 1 one gets μ_{τ̃_0} = 1, μ_{τ̃_0c} = −1, μ_{τ̃} = μ_{τ̃c} = 0, so λ_{w,σ} − λ^∨_{w,σc} = (0) for every σ and μ̃ is not CTG. With '+', raising λ̃_{τ_0,1} by a moves the right-hand side by ±a for each of the finitely many w, so the proof's last sentence goes through and Lemma 4.3.6 stands.
sourceIssues.printed: The source gives a sufficient condition for a dominant μ̃ ∈ (ℤ^{2n}_+)^{Hom(F⁺,E)} to be CTG: every w ∈ W^P must satisfy (4.3.7) Σ_{i=1}^n (μ_{w,τ̃,i} − μ_{w,τ̃c,i}) ≠ Σ_{i=1}^n (μ_{w,τ̃_0,i} − μ_{w,τ̃_0c,i}).

review.reason: The minus sign in (4.3.7) on ACC 974 gives the total of the unitary row, not the conjugate paired-sum test. For n=1 and two embeddings, unitary rows (1,1) and (0,0) satisfy the printed inequality for every shuffle, but the identity shuffle has paired sums zero at both embeddings and is not CTG. Replacing minus by plus gives the stated sufficient criterion: failure of CTG would force all those sums to equal n times the same integer. The finite-shuffle perturbation argument then works.

sourceIssues.locator: §5.4, proof of Lemma 5.4.8, the verification that λ̃_i is CTG, p. 1017 (also in arXiv v2)
sourceIssues.correction: It suffices to show that μ̃_{τ,n+j} − μ̃_{τ,j} (1 ≤ j ≤ n) is not independent of j, for μ̃ = w(λ̃_i + ρ) − ρ; equivalently, that the 2n entries of λ̃_i + ρ cannot be split into two n-element sets, one a translate of the other. The 'look modulo M' argument proves this for n ≥ 2 when applied to differences instead of sums: since 2a_i ≡ M/4 mod M, a difference between the two blocks of λ̃(a_i) + ρ is ≡ ±M/4 up to 2n − 1 modulo M, and these are pairwise distinct; a difference within a block is ≡ 0 up to 2n − 1; and a difference within the first block (of size < nM) never equals one within the second (a nonzero multiple of nM up to 2n − 1). So a translate-split would pair the 2n entries inside one block of n entries, which is impossible. (The multiset I′ should likewise be formed from the entries of λ̃(a_i), which is what I′_1, I′_2, I′_3 list.)
sourceIssues.reason: By Definition 4.3.5 and λ^∨_{τ,i} = −λ_{τ,n+1−i}, CTG says that no λ_w satisfies λ_{w,τ,i} + λ_{w,τc,n+1−i} = i_0 for all τ and i, and under (2.2.2) this sum is μ̃_{τ,n+i} − μ̃_{τ,i}. The printed quantity μ̃_{τ,j} + μ̃_{τ,2n+1−j} equals λ_{w,τ̃,n+1−j} − λ_{w,τ̃c,n+1−j}, a different condition, and for n ≥ 3 the multiplicity criterion does not imply CTG: entries 0, 1, 3, 10, 11, 13 (n = 3) have no pair-sum of multiplicity 3, yet split as {0, 1, 3} and {10, 11, 13} = {0, 1, 3} + 10, which makes λ_w pure. (For n = 2 the two conditions coincide.) The lemma's conclusion survives for n ≥ 2 by the repaired argument, and a direct computation for 2 ≤ n ≤ 7 and several p agrees.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 1.4, p. 1241, and its proof in the final paragraph of §4 (after Remark 4.4), p. 1274. The cited result is ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2(4): Ann. of Math. 197 (2023), p. 1030, and arXiv:1812.09999v1, p. 109. The v1 numbering (Definition 6.2.28) is the one Qian cites.; finding scoped to the NSF Springer online-first copy; journal pages are a concordance, not printed in that PDF; physical NSF PDF pages 3 and 36.
sourceIssues.correction: Add the hypothesis l > n to Theorem 1.4. This is the second sentence of condition (4) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2; the fourth hypothesis of Theorem 1.4 copies only the first sentence. With l > n added, the proof on p. 1274 works as written. For odd primes l < n with l ∤ n, the paper does not prove Theorem 1.4 (the case l | n is already excluded by the enormity hypothesis). Proving it there would need an ordinary automorphy lifting theorem for such l. Neither ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 nor its subsequent adequate-image version (Miagkov–Thorne, arXiv:2203.04520v2, Theorem 1.3) provides one: both require p > n.
sourceIssues.reason:
**How the proof goes.** On p. 1274, Theorem 1.1 is used to make r̄|G_{F'} ι-ordinarily automorphic, and then ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 is applied at p = l to ρ = r|G_{F'}. The paper says that conditions (3) and (4) of that theorem, apart from decomposed genericity, "follow from the corresponding conditions of r̄".

**The missing condition.** Condition (4) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 reads: "There exists σ ∈ G_F − G_F(ζ_p) such that ρ̄(σ) is a scalar. We have p > n." This is the published text on p. 1030, and it is the same in arXiv v1, p. 109. The fourth hypothesis of Theorem 1.4 reproduces the first sentence and drops the second. Nothing in the hypotheses of Theorem 1.4 implies l > n:
- The enormity hypothesis excludes only l | n. ACC+ notes after Definition 6.2.29 that ad⁰ contains the scalars when p | n.
- Enormity puts no lower bound on l in terms of n. For l ∤ n, large subgroups such as SL_n(F_{l^r}) with r large are enormous.
- The other hypotheses (ordinarity, decomposed genericity, the scalar element) do not involve n.

**The bound is needed in ACC+.** The bound p > n is not a removable formality. It is used in the proof of Theorem 6.1.2 in §6.6: at the Ihara-avoidance places, n pairwise distinct characters trivial modulo the uniformiser are chosen, and §6.2.15 on level-raising deformations assumes p > n.

**What is affected.** For odd primes l < n with l ∤ n, Theorem 1.4 is asserted without proof. The first such case is n = 4, l = 3. No counterexample is known, and the statement may well be true there. So this is a gap in the range of a stated result, not a false statement.

**What is not affected.** With l > n added, the published argument proves the theorem. Theorem 1.1 is also unaffected: there ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 is applied at the auxiliary prime l′, which Proposition 4.1 (p. 1269) chooses with l′ > 2ln + 5 > n.

**Defence considered.** The introduction (p. 1241) says Theorem 1.4 is obtained by combining Theorem 1.1 with ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. One could read that as importing the cited theorem's hypotheses implicitly. This reading does not hold up: Theorem 1.4 lists its hypotheses explicitly, copying conditions (1)–(4) of the cited theorem except for this one sentence, and the proof asserts outright that those conditions follow.

**Version history and later use.** arXiv v1 has the same omission, and there Theorem 1.4 says only "Let l be a prime number". The journal version added "odd" but not l > n. One later paper applies Theorem 1.4 as printed under the sole restriction p ∤ 2n (A'Campo, Rigidity of automorphic Galois representations over CM fields, arXiv:2202.14022v4, Corollary 1.0.5), so it inherits the gap for odd p < n.

sourceIssues.correction:
Hypothesis (5) of ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2 needs a regular algebraic cuspidal π that is ι-ordinary at every place above the prime, in the sense of Geraghty's Definition 5.3. An automorphic lift that is only ordinary as a Galois representation is not enough. So "ordinarily automorphic" has to be defined on the automorphic side, as in the published Definition 1.3 (p. 1241), and both applications of Theorem 6.1.2 need that input.

(i) The auxiliary prime l′. Sym^{n−1} r_{E,l′}|G_{F′} is polarizable and ordinary above l′, because E has good ordinary reduction at l′. Geraghty's Lemma 5.9 then gives ι′-ordinary automorphy (published, p. 1273).

(ii) V_{λ,t}, which is not polarizable. Prove ι-ordinarity directly, as in the published Lemma 4.3.
- Write V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π) with ι′ compatible with ι, so that V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π).
- At each v | l we have v(t) < 0, and Lemma 3.12 shows that WD(V_{λ′,t}|G_{F′_v}) is a single Jordan block.
- Varma's bound WD(r_{l′,ι′}(π)|G_{F′_v})^{F-ss} ≺ ι′^{−1}rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) compares partial sums of block sizes, and the two sides have the same semisimplification. So rec(π_v|det|^{(1−n)/2}) is also one block, and π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|^{(1−n)/2}) is a twist of Steinberg.
- The labelled Hodge–Tate weights are consecutive, so the automorphic weight is parallel. Geraghty's ordinarity conditions for this Steinberg representation then scale linearly in j, and they reduce to the single condition at j = n on val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(ϖ_v)^n) = val_l(ι^{−1}φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)).
- That condition is fixed by the continuous, hence unit-valued, l-adic character r_{l,ι}(φ_π) = det r_{l,ι}(π)·ε^{n(n−1)/2}, whose Hodge–Tate weights are nλ_τ.

So V_{λ,t} ⊗ χ_1^{−1} is ι-ordinarily automorphic, and hypothesis (5) holds in the proof of Theorem 1.4. The Galois-side ordinarity taken from the companion preprint (v1 Lemma 3.10(4)) is then no longer needed, and the published version drops it. The conclusions "ordinarily automorphic" in the published Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 are to be read as ι-ordinary automorphy in the sense of the revised Definition 1.3.
sourceIssues.reason:
In arXiv v1, Definition 1.3 (p. 2) calls r̄ ordinarily automorphic when it has an automorphic lift that is "potentially semistable and ordinary with regular Hodge-Tate weights" at every place above l. This is a condition on the Galois side. Under this definition the last sentence of the proof of Theorem 1.1 (p. 24) is correct: Lemma 3.10(4), from the companion preprint, gives Galois ordinarity of V_{λ,t} when v(t) < 0.

The gap is where this Galois-side notion is used in ACC+ Theorem 6.1.2. Hypothesis (5) of that theorem requires π itself to be ι-ordinary in Geraghty's Hecke-theoretic sense. This happens twice:
- On p. 24, for Sym^{n−1} r_{E,l′} ("ordinarily automorphic by our choice of l′").
- On p. 26, for V_{λ,t} ⊗ χ_1^{−1} in the proof of Theorem 1.4, where only conditions (3) and (4) are checked.

Passing from "automorphic and ordinary at l as a Galois representation" to "π is ι-ordinary" is the converse direction of ordinary local–global compatibility. Geraghty's Lemma 5.9 proves it only for polarizable representations. ACC+ Theorem 5.5.1 and Corollary 5.5.2 give only the opposite direction. The Sym^{n−1} case is polarizable, so a citation repairs it. V_{λ,t} is built from a character of H_0 chosen to break self-duality, so it is not known to be polarizable, and it needs a new argument.

The published version identifies exactly this problem in Remark 4.4 (p. 1274), crediting J. Thorne, and supplies Lemma 4.3. I checked Lemma 4.3 against Varma's Definition 1 and Theorem 1 (arXiv:1411.2520):
- A one-block Galois side forces a one-block automorphic side, because (n) is maximal for the order and the semisimplifications agree.
- For a twist of Steinberg with parallel weight, the conditions for 1 ≤ j ≤ n are proportional to j, so only j = n matters.
- The j = n condition says that the normalised central Hecke eigenvalue is an l-adic unit. That follows from r_{l,ι}(φ_π) being a continuous l-adic character.

Small case: n = 2, F′_v = Q_l, λ_τ = 0, the Tate-curve shape. Here r_{l,ι}(φ_π) has Hodge–Tate weight 0, so φ_π has finite order and ψ_v(l)^2 is a unit. Hence π_v = Sp_2(ψ_v|·|^{−1/2}) has a unit U_l-eigenvalue and is ι-ordinary, consistent with the ordinarity of a Tate curve.

The gap therefore affects only proofs. The published version proves Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 in the stronger, automorphic-side sense. Its new restriction to odd l comes from §2 and is unrelated to this point. The phrase "ordinarily automorphic" on its own does not show where the gap is, so the quotation above cites the sentences that invoke Theorem 6.1.2.

A separate bookkeeping remark on Lemma 4.3 (p. 1273), outside this finding: the paper's normalisations are the geometric Artin map and Hodge–Tate weight −1 for the cyclotomic character, as in the proof of Lemma 3.11. With these, a unit-valued l-adic character with labelled Hodge–Tate weights k_τ satisfies val_l(ι^{−1}φ_v(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{k_τ}). For example, with n = 1, φ = ‖·‖^{−M} and r = ε^{−M}, both sides equal f_v·M. So the exponent −nλ_τ printed there should carry the sign that matches Geraghty's normalisation of the target. Since the same exponent is printed on both sides, the conclusion is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.3, first paragraph, p. 1273; finding scoped to the NSF Springer online-first copy; journal pages are a concordance, not printed in that PDF; physical NSF PDF pages 35.
sourceIssues.correction:
Under the hypotheses of Lemma 4.3, the only comparison available is V_{λ′,t}^{ss} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π). Here ι′ is chosen so that ι′ (through λ′) and ι (through λ) induce the same complex embedding of ℚ(ζ_N). The comparison follows from the equality of Frobenius characteristic polynomials across the compatible system, together with Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt, because r_{l′,ι′}(π) is semisimple.

Replace the sentence by the following argument, which needs no new hypothesis.
1. By Lemma 3.12 (with v(t) < 0), the Frobenius-semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation of V_{λ′,t}|G_{F′_v} is Sp_n(ψ) for a character ψ of W_{F′_v}. Its Weil-group semisimplification is therefore the segment ψ, ψ|·|, …, ψ|·|^{n−1}.
2. The semisimplified Weil–Deligne representation depends only on the semisimplification of the Galois representation. So WD(r_{l′,ι′}(π)|G_{F′_v})^{ss} is the same segment.
3. By Varma's Theorem (1ss), which applies because v ∤ l′, the same holds for ι′^{−1}rec_{F′_v}(π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2})^{ss}. Hence the cuspidal support of π_v|det|_v^{(1−n)/2} is a single segment of n characters.
4. Since π is cuspidal, π_v is generic. By Zelevinsky's classification, a generic irreducible representation is an irreducible product δ(Δ_1) × ⋯ × δ(Δ_k) of essentially square-integrable representations whose segments are pairwise unlinked. Splitting one segment into k ≥ 2 pieces always produces two juxtaposed pieces, which are linked. So k = 1.
5. Hence π_v ≅ Sp_n(ψ_v|·|^{(1−n)/2}) is Steinberg, without using Varma's monodromy bound.

Alternatively, at the one place where the lemma is applied, in the proof of Theorem 1.1 (pp. 1272–1273), V_{λ′,t} is irreducible. This is because ρ = V_{λ′,t} ⊗ χ̃_2^{−1} has absolutely irreducible reduction Symm^{n−1} r̄_{E,l′}|G_{F′}. So V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π), and the printed isomorphism holds there.
sourceIssues.reason:
Lemma 4.3 assumes only that V_{λ,t} is automorphic. In the sense of Definition 1.3 this means V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π). Comparing Frobenius polynomials across the compatible system then gives only V_{λ′,t}^{ss} ≅ r_{l′,ι′}(π).

The representation r_{l′,ι′}(π) is semisimple by construction (p. 1240; Varma, Introduction). But V_{λ′,t} is not known to be semisimple, since semisimplicity of the étale cohomology of the Dwork fibre is not known.

Maximal monodromy does not pass to the semisimplification. A nonzero proper G_{F′}-stable subspace W of V_{λ′,t} is inertia-stable, hence N-stable, so it is some ker N^k. Then N on W ⊕ V_{λ′,t}/W has two Jordan blocks. So the printed claim that WD(r_{l′,ι′}(π)|G_{F′_v}) has maximally nilpotent N is equivalent to V_{λ′,t} being irreducible. Nothing in the statement or proof of the lemma supplies this. With a smaller N on the Galois side, Varma's bound ≺ gives no information, so the printed deduction fails in the generality of the lemma.

Attempts to defend the paper:
- V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π) does not imply irreducibility of r_{l,ι}(π). The non-polarizable case is exactly the setting of the paper.
- Monodromy density for the family gives irreducibility only for generic t, not for every t with v(t) < 0.
- The gap is filled only at the lemma's application in the proof of Theorem 1.1. There the residual representation of V_{λ′,t} ⊗ χ̃_2^{−1} is stated on p. 1272 to be absolutely irreducible, and Theorem 6.1.2 of ACC+ even gives V_{λ′,t} ≅ r_{ι′}(π′) directly.

The lemma remains true as stated, by the repair above. Its ingredients are:
- Lemma 3.12, which gives the Weil-group semisimplification as a single segment;
- Varma's semisimplified compatibility at v ∤ l′;
- Shalika's genericity of the local components of a cuspidal π;
- Zelevinsky's classification of generic representations, which forces the twisted Steinberg representation.

The remainder of the proof uses only V_{λ,t} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π), the Hodge–Tate weights of Lemma 3.11 and the central character, so it is unchanged. Lemma 4.3 and Theorems 1.1 and 1.4 are therefore unaffected; only the written proof needs repair.

sourceIssues.correction: In the conventions the paper uses, π has weight (λ_τ)_τ, that is, λ_{τ,i} = +λ_τ for all i. Both the identity to be shown and the identity obtained should read val_l(ι^{−1}φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_{τ:F′_v↪Q̄_l} τ(ϖ_v)^{nλ_τ}), where ψ_v(det α^{(n)}_{ϖ_v}) = ψ_v(ϖ_v)^n = φ_{π,v}(ϖ_v). For general j the condition is val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(ϖ_v)^j) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{jλ_τ}). Once both signs are corrected, dividing by n and multiplying by j works as before, the argument closes, and Lemma 4.3 holds.
sourceIssues.reason:
The page image of p. 1273 matches the quoted text. The paper uses the conventions of Allen et al. [1], Ann. of Math. 197 (2023):
- Art sends uniformizers to geometric Frobenius (p. 906), and HT_τ(ε) = {−1} (p. 907).
- For π of weight λ, HT_τ(r_ι(π)) = {λ_{τ,1}+n−1, …, λ_{τ,n}} ([1, Theorem 6.1.1(5)(b), p. 1029]).
- For the central character, HT_τ(r_ι(ω_π)) = Σ_i λ_{τ,i} and det r_ι(π) = r_ι(ω_π)ε^{n(1−n)/2} ([1, p. 987]).

The paper's Lemma 2.4 (p. 1250) and Definition 1.2 (p. 1240) use the same normalisation. The proof of Lemma 3.11 (pp. 1266–1267) uses it too: there V_{λ,0} ≅ ⊕_i Q̄_l(−M(a_τ)−i) on inertia, with weights {M, …, M+n−1}, and Lemma 3.11(3) gives the ordinary weight λ_{τ,i} = M(a_τ). So consecutive weights {λ_τ, …, λ_τ+n−1} mean λ_{τ,i} = +λ_τ.

The proof itself uses this convention. It computes the weight of r_{l,ι}(φ_π) = det r_{l,ι}(π)·χ_cyc^{n(n−1)/2} as nλ_τ, which requires HT(χ_cyc) = −1; with the opposite sign it would get nλ_τ + n(n−1). By [1, p. 987], weight nλ_τ also forces Σ_i λ_{τ,i} = nλ_τ, not −nλ_τ.

The last step has the wrong sign. Let φ be an algebraic Hecke character and let h_τ be the τ-weight of r_{l,ι}(φ). On F′_v^×, r_{l,ι}(φ)∘Art_v = ι^{−1}φ_v·∏_τ τ(·)^{a_τ}. Near 1 the character φ_v is trivial and ε∘Art_v(u) = N(u), which gives a_τ = −h_τ. The left side takes unit values, so evaluating at ϖ_v gives val_l(ι^{−1}φ_v(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{+h_τ}). As a check, take φ = ||·||: then r_{l,ι}(φ) = ε, and val_l(q_v^{−1}) = −f_v = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{−1}), whereas the printed rule gives +f_v.

The target identity has the same wrong sign. Suppose Geraghty labels weights dually, so that "(−λ_τ)" is literally correct in his notation. The target still cannot be right. At j = n the normalised operator is central, so its condition holds either for every π of these Hodge–Tate weights or for none, and ι-ordinary ones exist. Also, [1, Corollary 5.5.2, p. 1028] and Matsumoto (arXiv:2312.01551v3, Lemma 4.34(2), pp. 46–47, from Geraghty's proofs of Lemmas 5.4 and 5.7) apply Geraghty's Definition 5.3 to π of weight λ in the sense of [1] without any change. Matsumoto's criterion requires val_l(ι^{−1}χ_i(ϖ_v)) = e_v^{−1}Σ_τ(λ_{τ,n+1−i}+i−1+(1−n)/2). The constituents of Sp_n(ψ_v|·|^{(1−n)/2}) are ψ_v|·|^s for s = (1−n)/2, …, (n−1)/2, and for parallel weight the criterion reduces to val_l(ι^{−1}ψ_v(ϖ_v)) = val_l(∏_τ τ(ϖ_v)^{λ_τ}).

Both printed identities are false whenever Σ_{τ|v} λ_τ ≠ 0, which happens here: for n = 2, λ_τ = M(a_τ) = (N−3)/2 > 0. The two sign errors cancel, so Lemma 4.3 is unaffected. The passage does not appear in arXiv v1.

sourceIssues.reason: There are three slips. First, the paper has no Theorem 5.5.1; in [1] Theorem 5.5.1 is the local–global compatibility theorem for ordinary parts, so “or” should be “of”. Second, the remark restricts V_{λ,t} to G_{F′_v}, so v must be a place of F′; the paper states the same assertion with “any l-adic place of F′” on p. 1243 and in Lemma 4.3 on p. 1273. The superseded argument, at the end of the proof of Theorem 1.1 in arXiv:2104.09761v1 (p. 24), deduced ordinary automorphy from V_{λ,t} being automorphic and ordinary at the l-adic places when v(t) < 0 (arXiv:2104.09761v1, Lemma 3.10(4), the main theorem of [14]). The published paper also uses ordinarity of V_{λ′,t} at the l′-adic places (v(t) > 0 there), but only to make V_{λ′,t} automorphic through the lifting theorem; it says nothing about π at the l-adic places. The “local-global compatibility result in this direction” that needs polarizability goes from Galois ordinarity to ι-ordinarity at the same prime, and the paper applies it in that form ([8, Lemma 5.9]) to Sym^{n−1} r_{E,l′} on p. 1273. sourceIssues.correction: First fix the misprints: "Theorem 5.5.1 or [1]" should read "of [1]", and "l-adic places v of F" should read "of F′". Then make the deduction only when the residual representation V[λ]_t ≅ χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄|G_{F′} of V_{λ,t} is absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. Twisting by a character preserves both properties, so this is the same as asking that r̄|G_{F′} be absolutely irreducible and decomposed generic. That holds in the setting of Theorem 1.4, but not in general in Theorem 1.1. Under this condition, cite the single-representation result [1, Corollary 5.5.2], or equivalently [1, Theorem 5.5.1] together with [1, Lemma 6.2.11] after the soluble base change used in that corollary's proof. The conclusion then covers only the global points t produced in the proof, and only on the decomposition groups of F′ at places above l. For those points it gives the conclusion of the main theorem of [14]. It does not give it for every t of negative valuation over every finite extension of an l-adic field containing ζ_N.
sourceIssues.reason:
[1, Theorem 5.5.1] is stated on p. 991 and restated on pp. 1026–1027 of the Annals version. It concerns Galois representations valued in ordinary Hecke algebras. It carries the standing hypothesis that F contains an imaginary quadratic field in which l splits, and it assumes [F^+:ℚ] > 1, a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal (by Definition 2.3.6, an absolutely irreducible residual representation) and a decomposed generic residual representation. The version for a single automorphic representation is [1, Corollary 5.5.2] on p. 1028. It requires the residual representation to be decomposed generic and irreducible. That corollary was added at a referee's request and appears first in the June 2022 arXiv revision; it is not in the December 2018 version that the paper cites.

The remark presents its conclusion as a consequence of the proof of Theorem 1.1, where r̄ is only semisimple. For a reducible r̄, or one that is not decomposed generic, the residual representation χ̄_1 ⊗ r̄|G_{F′} fails these hypotheses. A polarized local–global result such as Geraghty's cannot replace them, because V_{λ,t} is deliberately not self-dual. Irreducibility also matters for a second step. Transfer from the auxiliary prime l′ gives only V_{λ,t}^{ss} ≅ r_{l,ι}(π), and ordinarity of the semisimplification does not imply ordinarity of V_{λ,t}, because the order of the characters in the ordinary flag is prescribed. An absolutely irreducible residual representation makes V_{λ,t} irreducible and so closes this step.

Defence: in the setting of Theorem 1.4 the remark is correct. The proof of that theorem on p. 1274 shows that r̄|G_{F′} is absolutely irreducible, using linear disjointness from F^{avoid}, and decomposed generic, using [1, Lemma 7.1.7]. The remark, however, is not restricted to that setting.

The phrase "another way of proving the main result of [14]" overstates what is shown. [14, Theorem 1.1] (arXiv:2103.00106v1, p. 2) proves ordinarity for every t of negative valuation over every finite extension of a local field containing ζ_N. The remark covers only the global points given by Moret-Bailly's theorem.

The remark is not used anywhere. [1, Theorem 6.1.2(5)] (p. 1030) needs π to be ι-ordinary, which Lemma 4.3 supplies, and does not need Galois ordinarity of r_ι(π).
